items.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
items.kicker: Thousands of vermilion torii, climbing the hillside
items.body: Free, open 24 hours. Genuinely empty 6:30–8am; the base is crowded by mid-morning and stays that way until the tour buses leave in the late afternoon. Go to the Yotsutsuji junction (~30–45 min up) — most day visitors turn back there, and the crowd thins sharply past it.

items.name: Kiyomizu-dera
items.kicker: The wooden stage over Higashiyama, daytime visit
items.body: Opens 6:00am; regular closing time shifts by season (≈18:00 outside special night-viewing windows) — check the posted hours on arrival. Admission {{fact:kiyomizu-dera-admission-500-yen}}. The 2026 autumn night illumination runs Nov 21–30 — after this trip's dates — so this is a daytime visit only.

items.name: Toji Autumn Illumination
items.kicker: The night illumination that actually falls inside these dates
items.body: Toji's own site confirms its 2026 autumn illumination runs Oct 31–Dec 13, 18:00–21:00 (last entry), admission ¥1,000, no reservation needed — unlike Kiyomizu-dera (Nov 21–30) and Eikando (night lighting from Nov 20), both of which fall entirely after this trip ends. It's a five-story pagoda lit against a pond, a short walk from Kyoto Station. ⚠ Fitting an evening here means trading time against the already-packed Sun Nov 15 schedule (dawn Fushimi Inari through the reserved Houshoan dinner) — see the ledger's traveler question before booking around it.

items.name: Nanzenji (Suirokaku aqueduct)
items.kicker: A red-brick Meiji aqueduct arching through a temple ground
items.body: November hours 8:40am–5:00pm (reception to 4:40pm), main hall/garden admission ¥600, per the temple's own site. Two independent firsthand accounts single out the Suirokaku aqueduct specifically as noticeably quieter early morning or in light rain than at midday — one visitor called it 'beautiful in the drizzle' rather than a washout, making it a solid wet-weather stop in the same Higashiyama corridor as Kiyomizu-dera and Gion.

items.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Tenryu-ji
items.kicker: A green-lit path, then a UNESCO garden next door
items.body: The grove itself is a free public path — empty before 8am, packed by 9:30. Tenryu-ji's Sogenchi garden next door gives the visit more substance than the grove alone: garden admission {{fact:tenryuji-garden-500-yen}} (+¥300 for building access), 8:30am–5:00pm (7:30am garden opening Nov 15–30).

items.name: Todai-ji
items.kicker: A 15-metre bronze Buddha, and the deer outside
items.body: The Daibutsuden (Great Buddha Hall) is open 8:00am–5:00pm in November, admission {{fact:todaiji-admission-800-yen}}. Nara Park deer cluster densest — and pushiest — right at the Nandaimon gate; two independent resident-blog accounts point instead to Asajigahara-en, just north of Ukimido pond, for the same deer with far fewer tourists in the way.

items.name: Kasuga Taisha
items.body: Main sanctuary worship is free; the inner special-worship area is {{fact:kasuga-taisha-inner-700-yen}}. Open 7:00am–5:00pm in November. Pairs naturally with Todai-ji on the Nara day trip — the connecting path is a pleasant walk, not a detour.

items.name: Osaka Castle
items.kicker: The keep and its moat, in the middle of the city
items.body: The keep is open 9:00am–6:00pm (last entry 5:30pm), admission {{fact:osaka-castle-admission-1200-yen}}; the surrounding park is free to walk. A late-morning visit avoids the sharpest crowds without needing an early start.

items.claim: Kiyomizu-dera's autumn illumination is a highlight of any November Kyoto trip.
items.correction: The 2026 autumn night-viewing dates are Nov 21–30, confirmed on the temple's own event page — this trip's Nov 13–17 window ends before it starts. The intake's assumed anchor event doesn't actually happen during the trip; Kiyomizu-dera is a daytime visit here instead.

items.claim: The Kansai Thru Pass (or its newer name, Kansai Railway Pass Lite) is a good multi-day pass for a Kansai trip.
items.correction: Its 2026 sales and validity window runs Apr 1–Oct 2 only — it isn't sold or usable at all in November. It also excludes JR lines entirely (no Haruka, no JR Special Rapid, no JR Nara Line), which limits it even in-season for an itinerary built on JR routes.

items.claim: Fushimi Inari's torii tunnel means hiking the full mountain loop to the summit.
items.correction: Most of the crowd — and most of the photogenic tunnel — sits below the Yotsutsuji junction, a 30–45 minute climb. The summit loop adds 1.5–2 more hours for a view most visitors rate as a marginal payoff.

items.claim: Gion is fully open for wandering and photographing geiko/maiko on the street.
items.correction: Since May 2024, private alleys around Kosode Koji carry a posted ¥10,000 fine for entry or photography — a response to tourists chasing and touching performers. The main public streets (Hanamikoji, Yasaka Shrine) remain open as normal.
